scribe_response.text: Tell me about something you are proud of. One thing I am especially proud of happened in the summer of nineteen, nineteen ninety-eight. That year the uh heat was terrible, and the demand for water in Abu Dhabi had never been higher. Our plant was running at full capacity, and the margin for error had almost disappeared. Then one of the main circulation pumps began to shake, and the vibration grew worse each hour. The manufacturer sent a message saying that a replacement would take six weeks to arrive. We did not have six weeks, because the city could not do um without that water. I gathered the best operators and mechanics in the control room, and we spread the drawings on the table. Everyone looked tired, and nobody offered an idea for a long minute. Then I remembered my days at the pump works in Coimbatore and Subramaniam with his steel rod. I asked a mechanic to press the rod against the housing and listen to the bearing. He heard a harsh grinding, and we knew the fault was in the bearing, not in the impeller. That was a smaller problem than we had feared, and it could be solved on site. We needed a certain kind of ceramic bearing, which we did not have in the store. What happened next? A young engineer named Faisal suggested that a neighbouring plant might um have a spare. I telephoned their chief and explained our difficulty, and he agreed to lend it that same night. Faisal drove two hours through the dark with the bearing wrapped in a towel on the seat. We worked until sunrise, with the pump opened up like a patient on a table. Lakshmi had packed flasks of tea and a box of sweet biscuits for the crew. We drank it sitting on upturned crates, too tired to speak. I fitted the bearing myself, and um I tightened the bolts in the sequence that Mister Hale had taught me. When we restarted the pump, it ran so smoothly that the operators cheered. Outside, the sky was turning from black to a pale grey. Faisal fell asleep on the bench with grease on his cheek. The vibration gauge showed um almost nothing, and I wrote the number in my notebook with trembling fingers. We had lost only nine hours of capacity, and the city never noticed. Nobody wrote about it in the newspapers, and that was uh exactly as it should be. Can you tell me more about that? The company later gave me a small award, a framed certificate with a gold border. But the real reward was the faces of the young engineers that morning. I felt then that the plant was a family, not just a workplace. They had seen that a crisis can be met with patience, listening, and a good neighbour. Several of them went on to lead plants of their own, and they still send me greetings. I am also very proud of my sons, who became a doctor and a software engineer through their own effort. Lakshmi and I gave them time and books, and they did the rest. Still, the pump night stays in my memory as the finest hour of my um working life. It combined everything I loved, which was careful listening, shared work, and a machine brought back to health. I do not claim any genius in it, only attention. That is the secret of most things worth doing. My father the schoolmaster would have understood it at uh once. He once told me that pride is simply the quiet gladness of a job done properly. I think of him whenever I remember that summer.
